text:
DET has been the better team at creating and limiting chances this season. The Red Wings generate 3.24 expected goals per 60 and allow 3.25, and they hold 51% of the expected goals at five on five. PHI sits at 2.15 for and 3.72 against, with 35% at five on five, and has scored just 1.25 goals a game while allowing 3.75. The model projects 3.15 expected goals for DET tonight against 2.74 for PHI. On special teams, DET has the edge on the power play (0.91 expected goals per game to 0.54) and also on the penalty kill (0.78 allowed to 0.69... wait, PHI's 0.69 is lower, so PHI is slightly better there). DET takes 4.7 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side power plays.

In net, both projected starters have been shaky so far. Dan Vladar (PHI, projected) is at -2.54 goals saved above expected this season with a .875 save percentage, while John Gibson (DET, projected) is at -3.14 with a .863. Last season both were strong: Vladar at +12.74 over 52 games, Gibson at +10.11 over 57. Recent form favors DET only modestly. PHI is 0-4-1 in its last five with 40% of the expected goals, and DET is 1-2-2 with 52%, though DET lost its last game 5-4 in overtime after taking just 33% of the chances.

The model likes Alex DeBrincat most tonight, at 39% to score and 26% for two or more points. Viktor Arvidsson and Dylan Larkin follow at 34% each to score. For PHI, Tyson Foerster has the top goal probability at 25%, and Trevor Zegras has the best chance of a multi-point night at 19%.
